# Slim-arm study (generated by `python -m rnd.slim_study`)

Variants (all with the R2c/D20 torque requirement):
- **V0** today: belt stages at pitch / roll / yaw / elbow, every cartridge on a KX twist-lock socket; GIM8108-8 at pitch +
  elbow (D20), GIM6010-8 at roll + yaw, DM-J4310 wrist pitch on a KX56.
- **V1** V0 with every cartridge **bolted** (6 × M4 through a flange into heat-set inserts) instead of a KX socket.
- **V2** V1 + **inline GIM8108-36** (36:1, 35 N·m rated, 103 N·m peak, ≈ 1 kg, 24 V SDC303) on the shoulder pitch and roll
  axes: no belt, no big pulley there.

Geometry and mass deltas are derived from the CAD dimensions (rnd/parts/kx.py, roll.py, arm.py) and marked ESTIMATE
where they depend on an unpublished drawing (the GIM8108 frame diameter). Torque checks re-run the existing models with
the variant's masses and geometry: whole-workspace margins (spring.py), the 20 lb hug (payload_study.py) and the laundry
basket (basket.py, full 3D twin statics).

| | V0 today (KX sockets, belts) | V1 bolted cartridges | V2 bolted + inline GIM8108-36 at pitch and roll |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shoulder dome width / height (mm) | 172 / 210 | 172 / 190 | 128 / 120 |
| Motor bump diameter (collar or flange, mm) | 113 | 90 | 90 |
| Elbow housing width (mm) | 110 | 98 | 98 |
| One arm, detachable piece (kg) | 4.26 | 4.03 | 4.39 |
| Workspace margin, rated / p95 (pitch, roll, yaw, elbow, wrist) | 2.43, 1.61, 1.79, 3.44, 1.68 | 2.51, 1.66, 1.83, 3.51, 1.71 | 4.18, 2.79, 1.83, 3.51, 1.71 |
| 20 lb hug, worst of pitch/elbow (rated ×, load 0.2 m out) | 1.82× | 1.84× | 1.84× |
| Laundry basket (floor pick, carry, bed): worst duty margin (≥ 1 passes) | 1.47 ✅ | 1.50 ✅ | 2.45 ✅ |
| Joint speed at rated, pitch / roll (rpm) | 20 / 27 | 20 / 27 | 48 / 48 |
| Actuators per arm ($) | 570 | 570 | 722 |
| Notes | tool-free cartridge swap (1 collar twist) | swap = 6 screws; −40 min build per arm (no D15 sockets); wrist KX56 gone, so D21's lift-off issue at the wrist goes with it | shoulder roll dome shrinks the most (no Ø127 pulley); 2.25× reflected inertia at pitch/roll (36² vs 24²): stiffer to back-drive by hand; +$117 per arm |

**Reading (2026-11-27):**
- Envelope rows are ESTIMATEs from the CAD dimensions (the GIM8108 frame diameter is unpublished); the torque, mass, speed and cost rows are computed.
- **Back-drivability is about the total reduction.** Roll today is GIM6010 8:1 × belt 4.44 = 35.5:1, so an inline 36:1 roll feels the same by hand. Pitch today is GIM8108 8:1 × 3 = 24:1, so inline 36:1 there is (36/24)² = 2.25× the reflected rotor inertia, noticeably stiffer when someone moves the arm by hand.
- The visible bulk is the shoulder-roll dome: the Ø127 80T pulley and the roll cartridge sitting above it. The pitch module is mostly inside the torso.
- **Recommendation (D24): V1 everywhere (bolted cartridges) + inline GIM8108-36 at the shoulder roll only.** It gets most of V2's slimming (shoulder dome ≈ 128 × 120 mm instead of 172 × 210), with the same hand-feel at roll, roll speed 27 → 48 rpm, +$61 per arm. Shoulder pitch stays on its belt (GIM8108-8 × 3).
